title: Vietnam Textile Sustainability Monitoring
thesis: Snowflake turns daily data from 30 wet-processing mills of a fictional Vietnamese textile dyeing and finishing group into effluent-quality, emissions-intensity, steam trap leak closure and grievance KPIs, 7-day effluent exceedance-risk scores, COD anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Effluent samples within threshold, environmental exceedances, emissions intensity and community grievances for 30 knit, woven, denim, printing and yarn dyeing mills in 4 Vietnamese cities.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it traces back to mill-day rows. Thresholds are internal demo thresholds, not regulatory limits.
The root-cause chart shows that indigo colour carryover at denim wash plants puts the most effluent samples over the threshold.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of mill sustainability KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which mills are likely to have the next exceedance?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each mill's probability of an effluent exceedance in the next 7 days, from COD, ETP hydraulic load, recent exceedances, asset age and mill type.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags effluent COD outliers per mill, and the forecast projects group-wide CO2e emissions for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: How healthy are the controls behind those risks?

talking_points: Effluent treatment plant (ETP) uptime and steam trap leaks closed frame the group's environmental control capacity.
Inspection completion against effluent within threshold by mill is a synthetic association, not evidence of cause.
The action memo is drafted from the KPI, exceedance, root-cause and risk tables only, and needs human review.
show: ETP uptime and steam trap leak closure cards
tabs.call_out: From KPIs to a reviewed action memo in one place

transition.line: What is happening at the mills right now?

talking_points: Live effluent COD and ETP hydraulic load readings land in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, from the Snowflake simulator or from AWS IoT Core through S3 and Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ALARM readings with an SOP hint and the mill's current risk band, then emails the mill environmental officer.
tabs.call_out: From effluent alarm to action in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over synthetic exceedance-response SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (IoT Core, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
